lines.text: GTA 6 heads back to a fake Miami. The real Miami has a party trick: its roads stand up to let boats through.
On the Miami River, a whole row of drawbridges open on signal for passing boats.
Many are bascule bridges. Bascule is French for seesaw, and that's exactly how they work.
Each road deck, called a leaf, pivots on a huge axle called a trunnion.
Behind the pivot sits a massive counterweight that balances the heavy leaf, like a perfectly even seesaw.
Because it's so well balanced, relatively small motors can swing tons of steel up into the air.
And boats usually win. By federal rule, these bridges open on signal, except during rush hours.
